scenes.vo: An old clockmaker sold me a watch that adds one hour to every day.
scenes.cap: An old clockmaker sold me a watch that adds one hour to every day.

scenes.vo: Twenty five hours a day. I couldn't believe it. So I used the extra hour for work. More emails. More meetings.
scenes.cap: 25-hour days. I used the extra hour for more work.

scenes.vo: After a month, I was more tired than ever. The extra hour was always gone, and I never knew where.
scenes.cap: After a month: more tired than ever.

scenes.vo: I went back, angry. Your watch is broken. The old man opened the back of it. It was empty. No gears. Nothing.
scenes.cap: I went back angry. He opened the watch. It was empty.

scenes.vo: He smiled. It never added anything. It only made you believe one hour was yours. And you gave it away.
scenes.cap: "It never added anything. You just gave the hour away."

scenes.vo: So now, every day, one hour belongs to me. No emails. No meetings. Which hour of your day is yours?
scenes.cap: Now one hour a day is mine. Which hour is yours?
